observed.facings.png: Three facings on one shared scale. South: a pale, segmented, maggot-like grub seen end-on, nose toward the camera. Its body recedes up the image in five ringed segments. A large round pink-red mouth ringed with tiny teeth sits at the front, and stubby fleshy lobes stick out sideways on every segment. The back is mottled dark brown with glowing amber-gold spots. East: a long, low side profile of the same grub with about eight segments, stubby prolegs underneath and the round socket mouth at the right (front) end. Its back carries the same dark mottling and glowing spots, and the tail tapers to the left. North: the same grub from behind. The segments recede up the image, the rear end is a rounded, ringed pale stump and there is no mouth or eyes. Dark spotted backs and side lobes match the south view. No ground, root or tree is drawn in any facing.
observed.south.png: Front view of the grub: a round toothed sucker-mouth at the bottom centre faces the camera, with the ringed body stacked behind and above it. Pale cream underside, dark brown backs with glowing gold spots, side lobes per segment. Clean alpha.
observed.east.png: Side profile: a long, flat-bottomed, ground-hugging grub, straight rather than curled. A wide open circular mouth at the right end, small conical prolegs along the belly, dark spotted back, tapering tail at left. Clean alpha.
observed.north.png: Rear view: segments recede away from the camera, ending at a blunt, ringed, mouthless rear at the bottom. Dark spotted backs and paired side lobes. No face or eyes. Clean alpha.
observed.scale.png: Beside the vanilla human at max zoom, the grub is a tiny strip about a third of a cell long, lying low. At normal play (32 px/cell) it is a few-pixel speck next to the rat.

SOUTH_FRONT.seen: South shows the round socket mouth facing the camera at the bottom, with the body receding behind it: a front view at the game's angle.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North ends in a blunt, ringed, mouthless rear stump. There are no eyes and no mouth.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: South and north show the long body foreshortened along the camera's line of sight, segments stacked upward with the end face visible. That is the angled game camera, not a top-down plan view. East is a true profile.

SAME_SIZE.seen: The 176% height spread comes from the pose. A long, low worm is short and wide in profile (east, 55 px tall) and tall when foreshortened lengthwise (south/north about 145–152 px). Segment widths and the size of the mouth ring match across facings, so the body is the same size.

SAME_ANIMAL.seen: Every facing has the same cream body, dark mottled backs with glowing gold spots and side lobes. The mouth is on the front in south and east and absent in north.

SIGNATURE.seen: The socket mouth, the defining feature of a 'socket-mouthed grub', is big and legible on south and east. The grub is low to the ground and has no wings.

ALIEN.seen: The base form is a grub, but the glowing gold dorsal spots, the lamprey-like round toothed socket mouth and the paired fleshy lobes make it read as an invented creature, not a plain beetle larva.

DEPARTURES.seen: 1 socket mouth as the dominant head feature: PRESENT (south/east). 2 latched onto a root, feeding: ABSENT (no root; the mouth gapes open in empty air). 3 at ocular-tree roots bearing eye-like structures: ABSENT (no root mass drawn). 4 wingless, ground-hugging, pressed low and not C-curled: PRESENT (east is a straight, flat-bellied profile). Departures 2 and 3 describe scenery, which the alpha rule forbids on a creature sprite, so they may not belong on a body sprite at all.

STYLE.seen: Painterly, with soft shading, ring texture on the flesh and a fine dark outline. No cute face or glossy eyes, and it is not cel-shaded. Reads like vanilla RimWorld's insectoid larvae.

OURS.seen: Original art: no vanilla or other-mod animal is recognisable.

ALPHA.seen: Checkerboard shows through around every facing. No ground, root, shadow or halo, and the code confirms real alpha.

SCALE.seen: The grub is tiny beside the human (drawSize 0.32), which fits a small grub working tree roots. It is somewhat smaller than the rat.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it is a pale speck a few pixels long with no readable mouth or spots. Advisory only.

reply.needs_call_why: Departures 2 and 3 ask for a root and an ocular-tree root mass. Drawing those would break the alpha/no-scenery rule for a creature sprite. A human should decide whether those departures apply to the body sprite or belong to the tree's art.
proposals: Departures generated for creatures should not demand scenery (roots, trees, ground). Write them as body features only, or move the scenery lines to the related plant/building subject, so they don't conflict with the real-alpha rule.

request.prompt: A single wingless sparkleech grub feeding at the base of an ocular tree, drawn as a RimWorld creature sprite in the painterly vanilla RimWorld style: realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. The grub is a pale, soft-bodied, segmented larva. Its body is long and low, belly flat to the ground, with a shallow, gently rounded back no taller than about a third of its width, and short legs splayed sideways close to the ground. It lies stretched out along the ground in a straight, extended line, uncurled. The head ends in a large, round, socket-like mouth that dominates the face, a ringed sucking socket with a flared rim, entirely unlike a beetle larva's chewing jaws. The head is lowered to ground level and the socket mouth is sealed tight around a thick root, the flared rim pressed flush against the bark with no gap, and the front body segments are slightly drawn back as the grub draws sap. The root belongs to an ocular tree: a short, twisted mass of pale-brown roots running along the ground under and ahead of the grub, with several round, lidded eyeballs bulging from the bark, each with a wet iris and dark pupil, clearly recognizable as eyes. Along the grub's back, the dark segment patches each hold a few small, bright, stolen eye-like glints, echoing the eyes on the roots. The grub and the root mass are the only elements in the frame, on a transparent background with no soil or scenery. In the rear view, seen from behind, the grub's back, tail and haunches face the viewer with the head hidden, and the eyed root mass is still visible beyond it.
